primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Prenatal alcohol exposure disrupts growth and neurodevelopment and can produce characteristic facial abnormalities, impaired cognition, and behavioral dysfunction.
vignette: A school-age child has growth restriction, smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, learning disability, and poor impulse control. The mother reports heavy alcohol use during pregnancy.
distractor_notes: Down syndrome has characteristic trisomy 21 features and hypotonia.
Fragile X commonly has long face, large ears, macroorchidism, and autism-related features.
Turner syndrome affects phenotypic females with short stature and gonadal dysgenesis.
Congenital hypothyroidism causes developmental delay without the classic alcohol-associated facial pattern.
key_expl: Growth restriction, characteristic facial features, and neurobehavioral impairment after prenatal alcohol exposure indicate fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Maternal rubella infection early in pregnancy can disrupt fetal organogenesis, classically causing sensorineural deafness, cataracts, and congenital heart disease.
vignette: A newborn has bilateral cataracts, sensorineural hearing loss, and patent ductus arteriosus after maternal febrile rash illness early in pregnancy.
lead: Which maternal infection most likely caused these findings?
distractor_notes: CMV commonly causes periventricular calcifications and hearing loss but not the classic cataract-PDA triad.
Toxoplasmosis causes chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and intracranial calcifications.
Parvovirus B19 can cause fetal anemia and hydrops.
HSV commonly causes neonatal vesicular, CNS, or disseminated disease.
key_expl: Cataracts, deafness, and PDA are classic congenital rubella findings.
objective: Identify congenital rubella from its classic triad.

sources.title: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
sources.support: CDC describes cataracts, hearing impairment, and congenital heart defects from congenital rubella.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes congenital rubella risks during pregnancy.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Vitamin B12 deficiency impairs methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, causing megaloblastic anemia plus neurologic injury from methylmalonic acid accumulation and myelin dysfunction.
vignette: A 68-year-old vegan has macrocytic anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, paresthesias, and impaired vibration sense.
lead: Which metabolite is expected to be elevated?
distractor_notes: Homogentisic acid rises in alkaptonuria.
Uric acid may rise in many conditions but is not a diagnostic B12 metabolite.
Galactose-1-phosphate rises in classic galactosemia.
Succinylacetone rises in tyrosinemia type I.
key_expl: B12 deficiency impairs methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and elevates methylmalonic acid.
objective: Differentiate vitamin B12 from folate deficiency using methylmalonic acid and neurologic findings.

sources.title: Vitamin B12 — Health Professional Fact Sheet
sources.support: NIH ODS describes B12-dependent methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and neurologic deficiency effects.

sources.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes macrocytic anemia and neurologic manifestations.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: A beta-globin missense variant substitutes lysine for glutamic acid and can cause mild hemolytic anemia with target cells and hemoglobin crystals.
vignette: An adult with mild chronic hemolytic anemia has target cells and intracellular hemoglobin crystals. Electrophoresis shows predominant HbC.
distractor_notes: Glutamic acid to valine is the beta-globin substitution in sickle hemoglobin (HbS).
Glycine to serine is not the characteristic HBB substitution that produces HbC.
Lysine to glutamate is the reverse direction of the HbC substitution and is not the disease-causing change.
Proline to glycine is not the defining beta-globin change in hemoglobin C disease.
key_expl: Hemoglobin C results from a beta-globin Glu→Lys substitution.
objective: Identify the amino-acid substitution in hemoglobin C.

sources.title: Hemoglobin C disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes HbC as an inherited hemoglobin disorder causing mild hemolytic anemia.

sources.title: HBB gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes HBB variants including hemoglobin C.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Defects in spectrin, ankyrin, band 3, or protein 4.2 reduce membrane surface area, causing spherocytes that are trapped and destroyed in the spleen.
vignette: A teenager has anemia, jaundice, splenomegaly, and spherocytes with a negative direct Coombs test.
lead: Which mechanism best explains the hemolysis?
correct: Reduced erythrocyte deformability causing splenic sequestration
distractor_notes: Complement lysis occurs in PNH and some antibody-mediated processes.
Heinz body formation occurs in G6PD deficiency.
Shearing causes schistocytes.
Heme synthesis defects produce microcytic/sideroblastic patterns.
key_expl: Spherocytes cannot deform normally through splenic cords and undergo extravascular hemolysis.
objective: Explain splenic hemolysis in hereditary spherocytosis.

sources.title: Hereditary spherocytosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes RBC membrane defects and splenic destruction.

sources.title: ANK1 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes ankyrin in erythrocyte membrane structure.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: X-linked factor IX deficiency impairs intrinsic-pathway coagulation and causes deep tissue bleeding, hemarthroses, prolonged aPTT, and normal platelet count/PT.
vignette: A boy has recurrent hemarthroses, normal platelet count, normal PT, and prolonged aPTT. Factor VIII level is normal.
distractor_notes: Factor VII deficiency prolongs PT.
vWF disease usually causes mucocutaneous bleeding and can mildly prolong aPTT.
Factor XIII deficiency does not prolong PT or aPTT.
Fibrinogen deficiency affects both PT and aPTT and causes broader bleeding.
key_expl: With normal factor VIII and hemophilic bleeding, factor IX deficiency indicates hemophilia B.
objective: Differentiate hemophilia B from hemophilia A.
clues: isolated prolonged aPTT with normal factor VIII

sources.title: Hemophilia
sources.support: CDC describes hemophilia A and B as factor VIII and IX deficiencies with deep bleeding.

sources.title: Hemophilia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes X-linked factor deficiency and prolonged bleeding.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Clonal JAK2 activation drives erythrocytosis independent of erythropoietin and often increases leukocytes and platelets.
vignette: A 59-year-old man has headache, aquagenic pruritus, splenomegaly, hematocrit 61%, low erythropoietin, and a JAK2 V617F mutation.
distractor_notes: Hypoxic erythrocytosis has elevated EPO.
Dehydration raises hematocrit without clonal JAK2-driven panmyelosis.
Essential thrombocythemia is dominated by thrombocytosis.
CML is BCR-ABL1 driven.
key_expl: JAK2-positive erythrocytosis with suppressed EPO is classic polycythemia vera.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Clonal megakaryocytic proliferation, often due to JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutations, produces persistent thrombocytosis and risk of thrombosis or bleeding.
vignette: A 54-year-old woman has platelets 1,100,000/µL, erythromelalgia, and a JAK2 mutation. Hematocrit is normal.
lead: Which marrow cell lineage is primarily expanded?
distractor_notes: Erythroid expansion dominates polycythemia vera.
Lymphoblasts cause ALL.
Plasma cells cause myeloma.
Neutrophil-predominant clonal expansion occurs in other myeloid diseases.
key_expl: Essential thrombocythemia is a clonal megakaryocytic neoplasm causing marked thrombocytosis.
objective: Identify the dominant lineage in essential thrombocythemia.

sources.title: Essential thrombocythemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes clonal platelet overproduction from megakaryocytes.

sources.title: JAK2 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes JAK2 variants in essential thrombocythemia.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Clonal megakaryocytes release fibrogenic cytokines, leading to marrow fibrosis and extramedullary hematopoiesis with massive splenomegaly and teardrop cells.
vignette: A 67-year-old man has massive splenomegaly, anemia, teardrop erythrocytes, and a dry marrow tap.
lead: Which mechanism most directly causes the marrow abnormality?
correct: Fibrogenic cytokine release from clonal megakaryocytes
distractor_notes: Autoimmune hemolysis does not cause marrow fibrosis.
Iron deficiency causes microcytosis, not a dry tap with massive splenomegaly.
Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome.
GPIb deficiency causes Bernard-Soulier syndrome.
key_expl: Abnormal megakaryocytes drive marrow fibrosis via cytokines such as TGF-beta.
objective: Explain marrow fibrosis in primary myelofibrosis.

sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes marrow fibrosis, splenomegaly, and myeloproliferative mutations.

sources.title: Myelofibrosis
sources.support: NCI describes primary myelofibrosis and fibrotic marrow replacement.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Clonal mature B lymphocytes accumulate in blood, marrow, lymph nodes, and spleen; smudge cells and hypogammaglobulinemia are common.
vignette: A 72-year-old man has asymptomatic lymphocytosis, generalized lymphadenopathy, and smudge cells on peripheral smear.
distractor_notes: ALL involves lymphoblasts and is more common in children.
CML shows granulocytic proliferation and BCR-ABL1.
Hairy cell leukemia often presents with splenomegaly and characteristic hairy projections rather than classic smudge cells.
Myeloma is a plasma-cell neoplasm.
key_expl: Older age, mature lymphocytosis, lymphadenopathy, and smudge cells are classic CLL.

sources.title: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
sources.support: NCI describes CLL as a mature B-cell malignancy in older adults.

sources.title: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes lymphocytosis and lymphadenopathy in CLL.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Profound defects in T-cell development or signaling with secondary impairment of B-cell function cause severe recurrent bacterial, viral, fungal, and opportunistic infections in infancy.
vignette: A 4-month-old infant has persistent thrush, chronic diarrhea, failure to thrive, and recurrent severe respiratory infections. Lymphocyte count is very low.
distractor_notes: Selective IgA deficiency is usually much milder and preserves T cells.
CGD causes phagocyte killing defects but not profound lymphopenia and thrush in early infancy.
Terminal complement defects predispose mainly to Neisseria.
ITP causes isolated thrombocytopenia.
key_expl: Early severe infections across pathogen classes with lymphopenia and failure to thrive are classic SCID.

sources.title: Severe combined immunodeficiency
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes severe early infections from combined T- and B-cell immune dysfunction.

sources.title: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency
sources.support: NIAID describes profound adaptive immune deficiency in infancy.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: C3 is central to all complement activation pathways and generates C3b for opsonization; deficiency causes recurrent severe infections with encapsulated bacteria.
vignette: A child has recurrent invasive pneumococcal infections and very low serum C3 with otherwise normal immunoglobulins.
lead: Which immune function is most directly impaired?
distractor_notes: IgE is unrelated to complement C3 function.
TCR rearrangement occurs in lymphocytes independently of complement.
NADPH oxidase deficiency causes CGD.
Platelet aggregation is a hemostatic process.
key_expl: C3b is a major opsonin; loss markedly impairs clearance of encapsulated bacteria.
objective: Identify C3b-mediated opsonization as the key lost function in C3 deficiency.

sources.title: Complement Blood Test
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes complement proteins as helping antibodies and immune cells destroy microbes.

sources.title: Complement Deficiencies
sources.support: NIAID describes recurrent bacterial infections in complement deficiencies.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Type IV hypersensitivity is mediated by antigen-specific T cells and macrophage activation rather than antibodies, producing delayed inflammation after exposure.
vignette: A patient develops an indurated erythematous skin reaction 48 hours after intradermal tuberculin antigen.
lead: Which immune mechanism causes the reaction?
distractor_notes: IgE-mediated type I reactions occur rapidly.
Antibody/complement cytotoxicity is type II.
Immune-complex deposition is type III.
Histamine release is characteristic of immediate allergy, not a 48-hour response.
key_expl: The tuberculin skin test is a classic delayed T-cell-mediated type IV hypersensitivity reaction.

sources.support: CDC describes delayed interpretation of tuberculin skin testing.
